children: Russian Urals crude premiums jumped to $8 per barrel against dated Brent for delivery to Indian ports, the highest since May, as lower crude supply from Gulf producers due to the
created shortages for refineries, three Reuters sources said.

Oil prices edged higher on Tuesday after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West Pipeline offline, raising fears that damage to energy infrastructure and transport routes could take longer to repair.

According to Reuters sources, cargoes of Russia's Urals are trading at a premium of about $8 per barrel on a delivered basis to India, compared with a premium of around $1 per barrel to dated Brent in August.
Premiums for Russian Far East ESPO Blend oil grade mainly purchased by China have also jumped significantly on high demand, fueled by a lack of Iranian and Middle Eastern oil supplies.
That also supported Urals values in India, as the countries are the two main buyers of Russian oil.

Urals prices are also being supported by lower loadings at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk this month. Traders said the port is still shipping oil below capacity due to high security risks and a lack of tankers.
In August, crude exports and transit shipments from Novorossiysk fell by more than half from July due to drone attacks, dropping to less than 350,000 barrels per day from 800,000 bpd.
